title: Chapter 108: The Secret of the Third Sick Hall
html:
I must have seen her somewhere before.

Chen Ge did not place unusual faith in his memory, but her face was distinctive. He snatched up his phone and hammer and gave chase, scattering rice beneath him. By the time he reached the corridor, the shadow had vanished.

Where did she go? The front door is locked, so she must still be inside the Haunted House.

He switched on his flashlight and noticed the rice formed a trail. It led to the far end of the first-floor corridor, where the boards covering the underground entrance had been raised. Wind whispered from below. Chen Ge moved the boards aside and entered Mu Yang High School.

There was rice left on the stairs, proof that the girl had entered the same scenario.

Her escape route is clear; she ran this way.

The scenario was vast, but the scattered grains guided him. Although the sets transformed the underground parking lot, its structural layout remained unchanged. The trail ended beside a load-bearing column.

Is she hiding inside the column?

The column stood directly beneath the Haunted House and supported its weight. As Chen Ge touched it, he remembered a story from his grandparents: every home had a resident spirit. Most were benevolent, but not all.

A benevolent spirit protected the house and its residents. A malicious one corrupted the family’s feng shui. Such spirits were usually deceased ancestors, though places like Fan Yu’s home proved exceptions existed.

The black phone’s description fit the legend. An invisible customer lived in the Haunted House, and it could be either friend or foe.

The girl hiding behind me earlier, could it be the spirit that protects the Haunted House?

The more he considered it, the more convinced he became. Circling the column, he found the first doll he had ever made propped against its base.

“Wait. Aren’t you supposed to be in my pocket?” He checked and found it empty. “Are you the one who has been living here with me?”

As he bent to retrieve the doll, he noticed a small hole behind it. He shone his flashlight inside. The narrow cavity, barely four fingers wide, contained a bracelet and a paper crane.

Neither item looked valuable. The plastic bracelet resembled a little girl’s toy, and the paper crane beneath it had been crushed out of shape. On the bracelet, three flowing characters spelled a name: Luo Ruoyu.

Why would there be a girl’s toy inside the underground parking lot?Chen Ge studied the bracelet closer. If this bracelet belongs to that shadow, then this should be the girl’s name.

The surname Luo. The Haunted House’s guardian spirit. A little girl’s toy.

The clues snapped together, and he remembered the girl’s face. She is Director Luo’s daughter!

He had seen her photograph while discussing the underground parking lot with Director Luo. She had been physically disabled, but her smile was radiant and pure.

Did she become the park’s guardian spirit? Why attach herself to the doll my parents left behind?The Nightmare Mission seemed to conceal a deeper meaning. Chen Ge carried the doll, bracelet, and crane back to the staff break room and took a photo album from a locked drawer. Its first page held a family portrait taken on the day the Haunted House was completed.

His father stood proudly in the center, grinning like a child. A school-age Chen Ge waited at one side, a trace of impatience on his face. His mother stood beside his father—but on closer inspection, one hand hung in empty space, her fingers curved around an invisible smaller hand.

There are four people in the picture?

Another photograph was stranger still. His father pointed at the Haunted House while speaking to him, and his mother crouched nearby with both hands resting on something invisible.

The album contained many similar pictures. A chill entered Chen Ge’s heart. As a child, he had always wondered why his parents left such large gaps in family photographs. Now he understood.

They sure were nice to the ghosts! It is probably because of them that I’m favored by the specters!

He had never imagined Director Luo’s daughter was attached to his parents’ doll, apparently for many years. As the park’s guardian spirit, she could not leave its grounds. That explained why the doll’s power worked only inside the Haunted House and New Century Park—and why it had done nothing when Wang Qi ambushed him behind Ping An Apartments.

Chen Ge closed the album and rubbed his temples. The mission held more than it first appeared. His gaze shifted from the doll and bracelet to the paper crane.

It was made from ordinary paper, stained with blood.

This paper crane does not look new; it should have been inside that hole for a long time already.

He unfolded the crane. Several words crossed the bloodstained paper: THE THIRD ROOM OF THE THIRD SICK HALL.

The Third Sick Hall?His heart quickened. Completing three Nightmare Missions would unlock a random Trial Mission. He had already hoped to choose the Third Sick Hall because it was the black phone’s only Three-Star Scenario.

The handwriting resembles my parents’. Why would they leave a location as a clue? Is the third room in the Third Sick Hall connected to their disappearance?He set the paper aside as another question surfaced.

The black phone said future Nightmare Missions would be randomized after the third. That means the first three were fixed.

The first mission opened a door to the other world. The second told me my parents are alive but missing. The third gave me a location. First it earned my trust, then offered hope, and finally pointed me toward an investigation. The three missions are connected, and each means more than it appears.
